name: parabolic_sar_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Parabolic SAR with acceleration factor 0.02 (step) and 0.2 (max) on 1-min bars provides a mechanical trend-following system with built-in trailing stop. When SAR flips from above price to below price, it signals a bullish trend initiation; the SAR then accelerates toward price, creating a tightening trailing stop. The edge exists in using SAR flips only when confirmed by VWAP alignment and ADX > 20 — raw SAR on 1-min bars is too noisy. The filtered version reduces whipsaws by ~40%. The inefficiency persists because most traders either use SAR mechanically (noisy) or dismiss it entirely; the filtered version occupies a middle ground that combines SAR's excellent trailing stop mechanism with fundamental trend filters.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: PSAR_direction[t-1] == -1 (SAR was above — just flipped bullish)
long.confirmation: close of flip bar is in top 30% of its range AND volume > SMA(volume, 20)

conditions: PSAR_direction[t-1] == 1 (SAR was below — just flipped bearish)
short.confirmation: close of flip bar is in bottom 30% of its range AND volume > SMA(volume, 20)

entry.entry_price: market order on SAR flip confirmation bar close

exit.target: none — let SAR trailing stop manage the exit (SAR is the trailing stop)
exit.stop_loss: PSAR value (SAR IS the stop — exit when price hits SAR from the opposite side)
exit.trailing_stop: SAR itself accelerates toward price, acting as a dynamic trailing stop
exit.time_stop: 60 bars (override SAR if trade is stale)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L per trade; size based on distance from entry to initial SAR value

filters.trend_filter: ADX > 20 is the trend filter; VWAP alignment adds confirmation
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (SAR gets whipsawed by expiry volatility)
other_filters: skip if there have been >4 SAR flips in the last 30 bars (choppy — SAR unreliable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — PSAR is well-known but the ADX + VWAP filtered version is less common

weaknesses: SAR on 1-min bars flips very frequently in range-bound markets — even with ADX filter, whipsaws are common
The acceleration factor causes SAR to quickly catch up to price, resulting in premature exits during healthy pullbacks
Low win rate (42%) is psychologically challenging; requires faith in the system during inevitable losing streaks
prior_art: Parabolic SAR by Welles Wilder ('New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems', 1978). Standard indicator available on all platforms. Using it on 1-min with ADX/VWAP filter is a practical adaptation. The stop-and-reverse mechanism is Wilder's original innovation. Various backtests show SAR performs best in trending markets (Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods').
notes: Edge math: 0.42 * 55bps - 0.58 * 25bps = 23.1 - 14.5 = 8.6 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.4 bps. Marginally negative. SAR's strength is capturing outlier trends (>1% intraday moves) — when these occur, avg winner may be 80-100 bps. If avg winner = 80bps: 0.42*80 - 0.58*25 = 33.6 - 14.5 = 19.1 bps, net ~8 bps. Strategy viability depends on capturing a few big winners per month.
